title: Resort Credit Issued Against a Granite Ridge Season Pass: Terms of Use
content:
Resort credit issued against a pass record is spent, not paid out.

**Where it may be spent.** It may be applied to any charge raised on that household account across the collective, taking the charge down before any payment method is presented.

**The validity period.** Resort credit is applied only when it is applied no later than its validity period counted in calendar days from the day the credit was issued. Calendar days are counted forward from the anchor date, the anchor date itself counting as day zero, every day of the week counting alike, and a calendar day is never mixed with a full 24-hour period; where the resulting boundary falls on a date that does not exist in the target month, the last day of that month is used. The comparison is not-later-than and the boundary day itself satisfies it.

**The smallest application.** A single application of credit must be at least the tier's minimum, and credit may be applied to part of a charge, leaving the remainder to be paid.

**The state of the record.** Resort credit is applied only while the pass record it sits on has not reached the cancelled or closed state.

**What it is not.** Credit is never exchanged for cash, never transferred to another household account, and never reinstated once its validity period has run out.

**Order of application.** Where several credit entries sit on one pass, the entry closest to running out is applied first.

### Basis questions the desk is asked

*May credit on one pass be applied to a lodging folio on the same household account?* Yes. The credit is applied to any charge raised on that household account across the collective.

*May a guest take 20.00 of credit against a charge on a Granite Ridge Summit Plus Pass?* No. That tier's smallest single application is 50.00, and an application below the tier's minimum is not made.

*Credit issued 364 calendar days ago on a Granite Ridge Summit Plus Pass.* That tier's validity period is 365 calendar days, so the credit may still be applied; on the day after the boundary day it may not, and it is not reinstated afterwards.

*Credit sitting on a pass record that has reached the cancelled state.* It is not applied, whatever the validity period still shows.
